title: Hooded cowl
subtitle: A cowl tube with a rectangular hood attached at the top back edge.
excerpt: A cowl with an attached hood knitted in two sections on 5 mm needles with aran-weight yarn: a cowl tube worked in the round followed by a flat hood panel picked up along the back top edge. The finished cowl measures 60 cm circumference and 25 cm tall, and the hood adds 30 cm of coverage from the nape to the top of the head.
sourceNotes: Victorian hood-and-collar patterns in Weldon's Practical Knitter (1880s-1900s), Internet Archive, combine a neckwear tube with an attached hood worked flat. This construction is an adaptation of that principle to a modern cowl silhouette.
heroPrompt: A finished hooded cowl in charcoal aran-weight yarn, photographed on a plain mannequin with the hood pulled up over the head, showing the cowl tube sitting at the neck and the hood covering the top of the head.

glossaryTerms.definition: Knitting a small circumference in the round on one long circular needle by pulling a loop of cable through the stitches at the halfway point.
Joining two parallel sets of live stitches by holding the needles together and knitting one stitch from each together before binding off. Produces a neat seam at the hood crown.
Drawing new stitches through the edge of a finished knitted piece to begin a new section. For the hood, stitches are picked up through the top back edge of the cowl tube.
A cast-on forming a neat elastic edge by using the tail and working yarn over two fingers simultaneously.

content.text: This is a cowl with an attached hood knitted in two sections on 5 mm needles with aran-weight yarn, finishing at 60 cm circumference and 25 cm tall for the cowl tube, with a 30 cm hood worked flat from the back top edge. The cowl section is worked in the round first, then stitches are
picked up
along the back half of the top cowl edge and worked flat up to the crown, where a
three-needle bind-off
closes the top seam.

The two-section construction was chosen because the cowl tube works most naturally in the round without a seam, while the flat hood panel needs shaping at the crown that is easiest on straight needles. The
magic loop
handles the cowl section; a straight or short circular handles the hood. The finished piece needs about 500 m (approximately 280 g) of aran-weight yarn.
What you need

items.name: Aran-weight wool or wool-blend yarn
items.substitutions: Wool or a wool-blend gives the best warmth and structure for the hood.

items.name: 5 mm circular needle, 80 cm (UK 6 / US 8)
items.substitutions: Two needles useful for the three-needle bind-off at the crown.

items.name: 5 mm straight or short circular needle

content.text: Gauge

18 sts x 24 rounds = 10 x 10 cm in stocking stitch in the round on 5 mm needles, blocked. The gauge is the same for both the cowl tube and the hood panel. One stitch per 10 cm off gauge shifts the cowl circumference by approximately 3.3 cm and the hood width by approximately 1.6 cm. Gauge determines whether the hood covers the head generously or tightly.
Stitches used

K (knit), P (purl) for rib edges. Stocking stitch in the round: all K every round. Stocking stitch flat: K on RS, P on WS. Three-needle bind-off: hold two needles parallel, knit one stitch from each together, bind off.
Pattern
Cowl tube -- cast on
Use the
long-tail cast-on

to place 108 stitches on the needle. Before beginning, calculate the tail: tail_cm = (needle circumference mm x stitch count) / 10 + 15. For 5 mm needles (circumference approximately 15.7 mm) and 108 stitches: (15.7 x 108) / 10 + 15 = 169.6 + 15 = about 185 cm. Leave a tail of at least 185 cm.
Stitch count check-in: after the cast-on you should have 108 stitches on the needle. Join to work in the round. Place a stitch marker.
Cowl tube -- body
Rib section (6 rounds): *K1, P1; repeat from * to end. (108 sts)
Body (54 rounds): K all stitches every round. (108 sts)
Closing rib (6 rounds): *K1, P1; repeat from * to end. (108 sts)
Bind off the front half (54 stitches) with a stretchy bind-off. Leave the back half (54 stitches) on a holder or spare needle.
Hood panel -- pick up and knit
The 54 live stitches from the back half of the cowl tube become the bottom of the hood. Work back and forth flat from these 54 stitches.
Stitch count check-in: you should have 54 stitches on the needle for the hood panel.
Row 1 (RS): K54. (54 sts)
Row 2 (WS): P54. (54 sts)
Repeat rows 1 and 2 until the hood panel measures 30 cm from the picked-up edge, ending on a WS row.
Hood seam

Fold the hood panel in half lengthwise so the two 27-stitch groups of the 54 live stitches sit parallel on two needles. Work a three-needle bind-off to close the crown seam: hold the two needle tips together, *K1 from each needle as one stitch, repeat until 2 stitches on right needle, pass first over second; continue to end.
Common faults

Hood sitting too far forward rather than covering the crown. This happens if the hood panel stitches are picked up from the front half of the cowl rather than the back half. Mark the back half clearly before binding off the front.

Crown seam pulling too tight. The three-needle bind-off should be worked at relaxed tension. A tight crown seam compresses the top of the hood and makes it look pointed. If the seam feels tight as you work it, switch to a needle one size larger for the bind-off needle.

Hood panel not reaching the crown of the head. The 30 cm hood depth covers an average head from nape to crown. If your head is larger or if you prefer more coverage, work an additional 4 to 5 cm before the three-needle bind-off.
Finishing

Weave in all tails: cast-on tail, front bind-off tail, and the crown seam tails. Wet block the cowl and hood gently: soak in cool water, press out water, and lay flat to dry. The hood panel should be blocked flat before the crown seam is sewn if you need to check the hood dimensions.
Care
Handwash in cool water with wool wash. Lay flat to dry. Do not wring or tumble dry.
What to try next

The basic cowl is the same cowl tube without the hood, which is a useful comparison piece. The snood is a shorter hooded neck tube in a similar construction with a gathered top rather than a flat seam.
